turns.user: For a 3D-printable mortar with w/b 0.32, s/b 1.2, binder 70 % OPC + 20 % class F fly ash + 10 % silica fume, 0.8 % PCE and 0.2 % cellulose VMA, predict the static yield stress and plastic viscosity.
turns.text:
I’ll check the mix conventions, predict both properties, and retrieve published analogue mixes to help interpret the results.
| Property | Prediction q50 [q10, q90] |
|---|---:|
| Static yield stress | **855 [67, 5,016] Pa** |
| Plastic viscosity | **7.11 [0.89, 27.07] Pa·s** |

Brackets show the 80% prediction interval. No inputs exceeded the training ranges. Although neither model was flagged weak, the returned cross-validation scores were slightly negative, so treat these as **order-of-magnitude guidance**.

For context, the published **M0PE** mortar reports **894 Pa** static yield stress and **6.5 Pa·s** viscosity ([source](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mtsust.2026.101398)). It has a different, slag-rich composition; retrieval matched properties rather than composition.

Assumptions: admixture percentages are product mass relative to binder; natural sand; zero specified rest time; 3DCP enabled. Tool defaults were age **28 d**, **comp_cube50**, and moist curing at **20 °C, 95% RH**.

Experimental rheology and printing trials are needed to verify the mix.
